nodes.label: SecretRef reference contract
nodes.rationale: Git-backed resources must reference secret material without storing secret bytes in Git; SecretRef is a typed, provider-neutral pointer resolved at runtime, rejected as a Git-backed Secret resource or provider-specific URI to avoid leaking deployment topology and creating rotation/deletion hazards.

nodes.label: CredentialsRef (future credential-semantics wrapper)
nodes.rationale: SecretRef is intentionally opaque (only answers 'where'); CredentialsRef will add protocol/type semantics ('what shape') without duplicating low-level resolution rules.

nodes.label: Namespace lifecycle (ADR-0002)
nodes.rationale: Namespace is hybrid: bootstrap namespaces are direct datastore writes to solve the chicken-and-egg problem of needing a repository before any git push is possible; all subsequent namespaces are git-backed to preserve reviewability, rejecting both a fully datastore-only model (loses reviewability) and a fully git-backed model with no bootstrap exception (no clean solution to the bootstrap problem).

nodes.label: gitstore-system well-known system repository
nodes.rationale: Auto-provisioned per namespace at bootstrap as the default authoring target for GraphQL catalog mutations that omit a repository name, avoiding the need for an external registry.

nodes.label: gitstore.dev/foreground-deletion finalizer protocol
nodes.rationale: Deletion must never silently cascade; dependents must drain before an owner resource is hard-deleted, mirroring Kubernetes foreground cascading deletion semantics.

nodes.label: Repository lifecycle (ADR-0003)
nodes.rationale: Repository is hybrid for the same bootstrap reason as Namespace; rename/transfer are rejected in Phase 1 because they would invalidate ownerReferences on all catalog resources and require a dedicated migration operation instead.

nodes.label: Product lifecycle (ADR-0004)
nodes.rationale: Product is fully Git-backed with no direct-datastore write path so downstream watch/reconcile semantics can depend on git as the single authoring source; direct datastore writes were rejected because they would create a split source of truth.

nodes.label: ProductVariant lifecycle (ADR-0005)
nodes.rationale: ProductVariant is the only purchasable SKU (variant-first contract, GH#143); spec.productRef is required and immutable to avoid orphan variants breaking the collection selector tree; co-creation semantics allow single-commit authoring of a product with its variants.

nodes.label: CategoryTaxonomy lifecycle (ADR-0006)
nodes.rationale: Synchronous strict parent-must-exist validation was rejected because it would break single-commit authoring of a full category tree; async ParentResolved=False plus layered cycle detection (instant self-loop at push, deep cycle detection by controller) balances authoring ergonomics against acyclicity guarantees.

nodes.label: ancestorPath materialized tree path
nodes.rationale: ancestorPath is derived, controller-managed state, not author-writable; storing it in git frontmatter was rejected because it would make re-parenting require two coordinated commits and create a conflict between authored and canonical paths.

nodes.label: Collection lifecycle (ADR-0007)
nodes.rationale: Collection deletion has no blocking dependents in Phase 1 (Products do not depend on Collections), so unlike other catalog kinds it needs no foreground-deletion finalizer drain step.

nodes.label: Selector-based membership model
nodes.rationale: An explicit membership list in git was rejected: it would create serialization contention among concurrently pushing authors; storing memberRefs in status was also rejected as it duplicates the query-time snapshot and creates status churn on every label edit.

nodes.label: File lifecycle (ADR-0008)
nodes.rationale: File is a manifest-plus-pointer, not an inline binary; storing payload directly in git was rejected for clone-time and history-noise reasons, and cascading binary deletion on manifest delete was rejected as an unsafe out-of-band side effect requiring an explicit future purgeFilePayload operation.

nodes.label: MediaAsset (separate catalog-facing layer)
nodes.rationale: Merging File and MediaAsset was rejected because it would couple byte-level storage decisions to presentation-layer edits; the two resources have different lifecycles and ownership.

nodes.label: Pluggable Datastore abstraction (memdb/ScyllaDB)
nodes.rationale: A single Datastore interface decouples GraphQL resolvers from the persistence backend so memdb (dev) and ScyllaDB (prod) can be swapped at startup via config without resolver changes.

nodes.label: Repository storage identity and fanout path strategy
nodes.rationale: Storage is keyed solely on the immutable repo_id (UUIDv7) rather than the mutable namespace/name external identity, so rename/transfer only touch database mappings and never move files on disk.
nodes.norm_label: repository storage identity and fanout path strategy

nodes.label: Two-phase reference resolution model (sync structural / async semantic)
nodes.rationale: Push-time structural validation is synchronous and blocking while existence/semantic resolution is async and controller-managed, allowing single-commit co-creation of related resources without strict push-order dependencies.
nodes.norm_label: two-phase reference resolution model (sync structural / async semantic)

nodes.label: GraphQL mutation delegation-to-git pattern
nodes.rationale: GraphQL create/update/delete mutations commit to git and wait for admission rather than writing directly to the datastore, preserving git as the single source of truth for all seven catalog resource kinds.

nodes.label: Native git:// Protocol Implementation Plan (obsolete)
nodes.rationale: Marked obsolete; scope narrowed so gitstore-git-service focuses on transport/repo-ops/hook execution points only, with schema-aware catalogue parsing pushed to external/API-managed hook workers instead of in-process domain models.

nodes.label: T152: Proper Git Protocol Solution (superseded)
nodes.rationale: Superseded by spec 004 (gRPC git service); the shared-volume MVP approach was explicitly a temporary unblock, with git:// network protocol as the originally planned but ultimately bypassed production path.

nodes.label: CI implementation options exploration for GitStore Actions
nodes.rationale: Tekton is recommended as the Kubernetes-native execution substrate to fit gitstore-controller-manager's existing direction, while Woodpecker-style server/agent architecture is recommended as the faster local-first alternative; Jenkins and heavy legacy CI systems were rejected as poor foundations.
nodes.norm_label: ci implementation options exploration for gitstore actions

nodes.label: GitStore Implementation Roadmap (phase-ordered backlog)
nodes.rationale: Recommends closing the admission/lifecycle/watch architecture proof before storefront work, because cart/checkout/inventory correctness would otherwise be built on unstable control-plane invariants; also flags that Git-managed Order/PaymentIntent research issues are misaligned with the documented datastore-only runtime resource model.

nodes.label: GitStore Pluggable AuthN/AuthZ Architecture Design
nodes.rationale: Chooses a shared HMAC bearer token over mTLS for gRPC inter-service trust in phase 1 because mTLS requires PKI infrastructure that does not yet exist; chooses OPA over OpenFGA for production AuthZ because OPA's Rego model maps directly onto the existing rbac-local YAML schema without requiring a new relational tuple store.

nodes.label: ChainedAuthN provider chain
nodes.rationale: First Allow wins and an explicit Deny short-circuits the chain immediately; an all-Challenge outcome is treated as an authentication failure rather than an anonymous request, closing a gap where unrecognized credentials could otherwise fall through to anonymous access.

nodes.label: Pluggable Identity and Access Design (target design, superseded)
nodes.rationale: Splits identity/access into three independently configurable planes (AuthN, AuthZ, UserDir) so resolvers only ever consume a provider-agnostic Principal and never parse raw provider token formats directly.

nodes.label: gix tree-editor eliminates clone-to-workdir pattern

nodes.label: Configurable pack size limit via Axum DefaultBodyLimit
